title: Ubisoft calls Skull and Bones 'AAAA' label puffery 🏴‍☠️
subject: skullandbones
description:
Did you buy Skull and Bones at $70? 👇

In a US consumer lawsuit filed under the Kansas Consumer Protection Act by player Jacob Himberger, Ubisoft's lawyers described CEO Yves Guillemot's 2024 description of Skull and Bones as a 'AAAA' game as 'classic puffery', arguing the company made no specific promises. The suit also claims Ubisoft sold a limited license rather than ownership. The case was moved to a federal court in California, where it was voluntarily dismissed in September 2026 and may be refiled; no court has ruled on the AAAA claim itself.

Sources: Game World Observer (Nov 26, 2026), 80.lv (Nov 27, 2026), Game File
Game footage/images © Ubisoft.

scenes.text: Skull and Bones' 'AAAA' tag was just hype, Ubisoft argues.
In 2024, CEO Yves Guillemot called it a 'AAAA' game on an earnings call, defending its $70 price.
Player Jacob Himberger then sued in Kansas under its consumer protection law.
Ubisoft's lawyers called the label 'classic puffery' and said the company made no specific promises.
The suit also claims Ubisoft sold a limited license, not ownership.
Skull and Bones spent over 10 years in development. No court has ruled on the 'AAAA' claim.
